Introduction and Policies
The purpose of this Risk Management Plan (RMP) is to describe measures to be implemented
by Kiros Energy Marketing ULC (Kiros) to prepare to respond to emergency situations in a safe,
effective, and timely manner to mitigate impacts to human health and the environment. The
accidental release prevention and emergency response policies for Kiros operating 967 NC Highway 211 E, Candor, NC 27229 (hereafter referred to as the Site), complies with NFPA-58
requirements for LPG storage, and it is the policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state, and local laws. If an emergency were to occur, it is Kiros policy to notify the Eagle Springs Fire Department (910-673-5673 or 911) and local emergency planning committee (LEPC) and request that they respond to the emergency.

This plan has been prepared to meet the requirements of Title 40, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 68 (40 CFR Part 68); the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Process Safety Management (PSM) Standard, 29 CFR Part 1910.119; the OSHA Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response Standard (HAZWOPER), 29 CFR 1910.132; Personal Protective Equipment General Requirements, 29 CFR 1910.133; Personal Protective Equipment Eye and face protection, 29 CFR 1910.134; Personal Protective Equipment Respiratory protection, 29 CFR 1910.138; Personal Protective Equipment Hand protection, 29 CFR 1910.120; the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1200.

Stationary Source and Regulated Substance
The Candor facility is leased/operated by Kiros Energy Marketing.  Kiros, or agents/contract operators working on behalf of Kiros, will not conduct any non-clerical activities inside any onsite buildings. Kiros will be offloading butane and propane from stationary rail cars into tanker trucks (or vice versa). Rail cars and tanker trucks will be managed to protect the humans and the environment. This plan establishes a framework for identification, assessment, control, and res

ponse among onsite and offsite personnel.
Kiros, or agents/contract operators working on behalf of Kiros, off loads liquid petroleum gas (LPG) from approximately 29,000 to 30,500-gallon capacity rail cars to 8,000 to 15,000-gallon tanker trucks (or vice versa). Trained on this plan and NRPA-58, Kiros employees/agents are present during all offloading of butane and propane from a railcar to a tanker truck.
Kiros worst-case scenario is failure of one of the 30,500-gallon capacity rail cars, which could potentially result in a vapor cloud explosion with an approximately a radius of 0.40 miles. The resulting distance to the endpoint extends off site, and public receptors are within distance to the endpoint. The alternative release scenario is a pull-away or piping break explosion. In either case, an estimated maximum of 1,750 gallons of LPG would be released. The resulting distance to the endpoint extends off site with an approximate radius of 0.10 miles, and public receptors are within distance to the endpoint 
Kiros complies with Environmental Protection Agencys (EPA) accident prevention rule, the OSHA PSM standard, and all applicable state and local codes and regulations. The rail cars are designed and maintained in accordance with NFPA-58 and state laws.
 


Kiros has never experienced an accident involving LPG that caused deaths, injuries, property or environmental damage, evacuations, or sheltering in place at the Site.

In the event of an emergency involving LPG, it is Kiros policy to notify the Eagle Springs Fire Department (910-673-5673 or 911) and request that they help respond to the emergency. Kiros will have coordinated a response plan with the fire department and invites the fire department to inspect the off-loading system and conduct a joint exercise with them to respond to any emergencies onsite.

There are currently no planned construction changes to improve the safety of the Site. However, continual training takes place with Kiros employees.
Accide

ntal Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
The accidental release prevention and emergency response programs in place at the facility are part of the high standards striven for by Kiros. These high standards include:
-	Operating in compliance with required environmental permits and regulations.
-	Operating and maintaining the assets in such a manner that unintentional releases are minimized.
-	Operating and maintaining assets in such a manner that the small releases associated with normal operation and maintenance will be minimized to the extent possible.
-	Correcting non-compliance found during regular audits of the facility.

Prevention Program
The Candor Facility operates under the guidelines of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Process Safety Management (PSM) Program. They also operate under the requirements of Program Level 2 in the RMP regulations. Analysis of the potential hazards of the process, training of employees, and emphasis on safety has helped avoid any serious chemical release accidents since operations began. Part of this program has also involved identifying and taking steps to avoid potential accidental chemical releases.


Five-Year Accident History
No incident resulting in onsite injuries, death or property damage or offsite impacts from a propane release has occurred at the Summit Siding Facility within the last five years.

Emergency Response Program
Kiros and the contract operator have documented emergency response plans and procedures in place at the Candor property to respond to and safety mitigate any release or accident involving propane. Included in the emergency response plan are measures to be taken internally by Kiros contract operators to control the release, if possible, and to make initial notification to local responders and to Kiros headquarters. Operator personnel at the terminal are trained to the Hazardous Materials Operations level as outlined in 29 CFR 1910.120 Hazardous Waste Operations

and Emergency Response. These employees may also perform activities under the specialist employee definition as defined by 1910.120. These personnel receive annual training on activation of the facility emergency action
plan, their roles in an emergency and accident notification procedures. To assure that the local municipal response agencies are familiar with Kiros emergency response procedures and copies of the all-emergency action plans have been shared with and reviewed by local responders. In the event of a significant release of propane that involve off site populations, these populations will be notified through the LEPC.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety
Compliance with the RMP Prevention Program coupled with the environmental, health and safety management systems, forms the framework for continuous safety improvement. Some of the key components of the safety program are:
-	The Management of Change provisions ensure that the potential safety and health impacts of any change made to process chemicals, technology, equipment or procedures are considered.
-	The Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) provisions serve as a tool to ensure timely evaluation of potential hazards, thereby leading to continual improvements in safety standards.
-	The Mechanical Integrity provisions ensure that process equipment and instrumentation are designed, constructed, installed and maintained to minimize the risk of hazardous releases, thereby serving as an integral part of the safety program.
Specific actions that will be taken in the future to improve the level of safety at the facility include:
-	Compliance audits will ensure that the level of safety protection at the facility is periodically being evaluated for improvements.
-	An ongoing dialogue with the local Fire Department will ensure a constant state of readiness to respond to any potential emergencies, as well as a means to implement improvements as the need develops.
